analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 23 Nov: Weekly; M&S d/g to Neutral; Unilever; Heineken; Brown-Forman
key_insights: S&P fell 3.7% and Nasdaq-100 fell 5.6% last week, the worst week since Mar-20, led by a fragile AI/capex narrative. NVDA fell 14% to an 18-month low on a report of an SEC accounting probe and SOXX fell 10%. Staples was the only sector in the green.

US futures are bouncing (Nasdaq +3%, S&P +2%) after Bessent warned the Fed risks overtightening. The desk draws parallels with Q4 2018, with a correction into a hawkish December Fed. Dec Fed is 93% priced for a 25bp hike, blackout runs 28 Nov to 10 Dec.

Thanksgiving week has averaged S&P +71bps over 30 years with a 63% hit rate, but in 2018 the S&P fell 3.8% that week. Desk expects a low-volume technical recovery without a definitive short-term catalyst for the AI capex story.

Marks & Spencer downgraded to Neutral, PT raised 1.1% to 470p from 465p. UBS sees FY28e EPS growth of 9% vs 12% consensus and expects revisions to pause as investment takes center stage. Re-rating needs a sustained FHB recovery, unlikely before H2'28e.

US Consumer Staples: XLP outperformed the S&P 500 for a seventh straight week (+240bps) but fell about 270bps in absolute terms. XLP trades at a ~15% premium to the S&P, the widest since 12/22. UBS sees limited downside to numbers but limited upside priced in.
Europe consumer sectors both lagged (SXQP -3.2%, SX3P -3.3%). Staples outperformance is driven by rotation out of AI/growth rather than improving fundamentals, prompting profit-taking debate.
Luxury is a stock-pickers' market. Richemont is a standout with FY27/28/29 EPS raised +5%/+4%/+3% and PT CHF215. Swiss watch exports held +10% y/y in Oct 3mma, with US +36%.

Sportswear read-across is tough for adidas and Puma after Nike Investor Day and JD Sports trading. UBS is at +4% FX-neutral 2027 sales growth vs +7% consensus and 9.1% EBIT margin vs 10.0% for adidas, leaving EBIT more than 10% below consensus. Nike trades at c29x FY27E P/E.

Remy is the positive actionable idea ahead of 1H27 results on 25 Nov. BNIC shipments, US sell-out and depletion commentary now align, and consensus embeds only ~€46m EBIT growth vs a €100m value-creation programme.

Unilever remains Sell. A Daily Mail piece argues the £50bn food sale could leave the £56bn health and beauty remainder open to a takeover. UBS is cautious on category concentration and valuation despite a 4-6% USG strategy.

Signet 3Q preview: UBS forecasts a 9c EPS beat and a possible FY27 guidance raise, with options implying +/-9.5% vs 11.5% historical average. Victoria's Secret has slight downside skew, with options implying +/-13.9% vs 10.1% historical average.
Luckin Coffee initiated at Buy with US$47.15 PT, a 20.4% revenue CAGR forecast for 2026-28E, trading at 12x 2027E P/E.
China vapour exports fell 3.3% in the last 6m to October, US exports -17.9%, which is positive for MO/BAT. UK combustibles fell 13.3% in October after the excise hike.
Japan Tobacco cut FY26 DPS 25% to ¥204 on Russian deconsolidation, targets about a 70% FY27 payout and >10% pa cFX operating-profit growth through 2027-29.
LVMH/Dior: Board approved conversion and Agache merger, shareholder vote 30 Dec, Arnault family tender at 95% of look-through NAV, final price set 23 Dec, offer to open in 1Q27.
Heineken is reportedly buying 300 Stonegate platinum pubs for about £300m.
